Task_Type.reason: Confirmed; the PDF supports two honest readings. T4: the stated aim is to characterise serum beta-synuclein longitudinally across CU, MCI and AD, and most of the paper is group comparisons, rate-of-change analysis, correlations with cognition and a comparison with CSF NRGN. T2: the paper also evaluates a beta-synuclein cut-point for MCI (Abeta+) converters versus stable MCI (Abeta+) within 5 years (AUC 0.90, sensitivity 76.9%, specificity 100% at 10.3 pg/mL), and it headlines MCI-to-dementia conversion prediction in the abstract Results and in the Conclusions. That satisfies the T2 condition (explicitly converters versus stable MCI) with a quantified discrimination figure. The conversion analysis is small (26 converters versus 5 stable), which keeps T4 the more literal core, but T2 is not ruled out.
